intro_html: Curled tighter than they'd like and shifting all evening. Large dog beds, most sized in centimetres, so a big dog fits on the bed, not around it.
description_html:
You know the look of a big dog on a bed that's too small: back legs on the floor, chin hanging off the edge, never quite settled. Plenty of beds sold as large are large for a spaniel. This large dog bed collection gathers beds with sizes for labradors, shepherds, retrievers and bigger, most of them listed in centimetres so you can check before you order; where a page gives no measurements, ask us first.

Large dog beds by how they sleep

Size gets them onto the bed. Shape decides whether they stay there.

  • If they sprawl flat out on their side, they want no walls in the way. Buttermere gives them 110 × 85cm of memory foam with no walls at all, 10cm deep. Wastwater is 127 × 91cm, with a raised head built into the foam.
  • If they lean with their back against the sofa, they want bolsters. Staveley and Melbreak are both 122 × 89cm, with three bolstered sides and an open front.
  • If they curl and tuck in, they want something on every side. Borrowdale is bolstered on all four sides over memory foam, with a waterproof inner liner under the cover.

Why a big dog needs more underneath

A heavy dog puts a lot of weight through hips, shoulders and elbows. Loose fibre filling shifts away from those points and packs down; foam spreads the load and keeps its shape. That's why most beds here are foam: memory foam, crumb memory foam, gel memory foam or profiled egg-crate foam, sometimes two layers together. Depth counts as well: Ennerdale is 24cm deep. Others are soft-filled by design, such as Troutbeck at 110 × 75cm. Most product pages say which kind of filling they use; where one does not, ask us before ordering. Our guide to what's inside the beds explains the foams in plain English.

Sizing a large dog bed

Measure your dog lying on their side, nose to base of tail, and add 15 to 20cm. Then check whether the bed's size is an outside measurement. Bolsters take up part of the footprint, so a bolstered bed needs more allowance than an open mattress. Between sizes, size up, or message us their breed and weight and we will tell you honestly which one fits. The size guide walks through it, and for giant breeds the XL and XXL dog beds go bigger again.

If they're slowing down

A stiff dog often hesitates at the edge of a high-walled bed. Open fronts like Staveley's and Melbreak's, or a flat mattress like Buttermere, leave nothing to climb, and our orthopaedic dog beds include more low-entry shapes. A bed is for comfort, not treatment; if your dog is in pain or struggling to get up, keep talking to your vet.

100 nights to be sure

A big bed takes up a lot of floor, so live with it before you decide. Every bed in this collection comes with the 100-night sleep trial. If it isn't right within 100 nights, we arrange free UK mainland collection and a full refund. One trial per household; damage and other exclusions apply. Some foam beds here also carry a 5-year no-flatten guarantee on the core, and where one does, its product page says so. Free standard UK delivery on orders over £40.

Large dog bed questions

What size bed does a labrador need?

Measure your own dog rather than going by breed: their length lying on their side, plus 15 to 20cm, compared with the usable area. Some beds list breeds by size, such as Patterdale's Large for golden retrievers, labradors and German shepherds. Treat that as a starting point.

Can I wash a large dog bed?

Most have removable covers; follow each sewn-in label and never wash or soak the foam. The Windermere and Bassenthwaite mesh beds have no cover at all and simply rinse down.

Still weighing it up? The Bed Finder begins with their sleeping position and recommends one bed.
